\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شلوغی} (sholughi)}{شلوغی (sholughi)}]{\fa{شلوغی} (sholughi) — the crowds, crowdedness; the rush}

\label{lesson:FA-C451-sholughi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a statue, then the Persian for a fountain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شلوغی}}
\textbf{\fa{شلوغی}} (\emph{sholughi}) — \textquotedblleft{}the crowds, crowdedness; the rush\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{از} \fa{شلوغی} \fa{بازار} \fa{خسته} \fa{شدیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Az sholughi-ye bâzâr khaste shodim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We got tired of the crowds in the bazaar.
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{sholugh} 'crowded, busy' + \emph{-i}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sholughi} is built from \emph{sholugh} 'crowded, noisy' and the noun ending \emph{-i}. The origin of \emph{sholugh} is not settled, and EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a statue, then the Persian for a fountain, then say \emph{sholughi} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نیمکت} (nimkat)}{نیمکت (nimkat)}]{\fa{نیمکت} (nimkat) — a bench}

\label{lesson:FA-C451-nimkat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a fountain, then the Persian for the crowds.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نیمکت}}
\textbf{\fa{نیمکت}} (\emph{nimkat}) — \textquotedblleft{}a bench\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پیرمرد} \fa{روی} \fa{نیمکت} \fa{پارک} \fa{نشسته} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pirmard ru-ye nimkat-e pârk neshaste bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The old man was sitting on a bench in the park.
\end{quote}

Also a school bench or desk.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nimkat} is a native word that EtymDB lists without older forms. It is usually analysed as \emph{nim} 'half' and \emph{kat} 'couch, bed': a half-couch.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ساکن} (sâken)}{ساکن (sâken)}]{\fa{ساکن} (sâken) — a resident, an inhabitant; living (in a place)}

\label{lesson:FA-C451-saken}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for the crowds, then the Persian for a bench.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ساکن}}
\textbf{\fa{ساکن}} (\emph{sâken}) — \textquotedblleft{}a resident, an inhabitant; living (in a place)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{ده} \fa{سال} \fa{ساکن} \fa{این} \fa{محله} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U dah sâl sâken-e in mahalle ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He has lived in this neighbourhood for ten years.
\end{quote}

Arabic plural \emph{sokkân} 'inhabitants'. Also 'still, motionless'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sâken} was borrowed from Arabic and is usually traced to Arabic \emph{sākin} 'dwelling, at rest'. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رهگذر} (rahgozar)}{رهگذر (rahgozar)}]{\fa{رهگذر} (rahgozar) — a passer-by}

\label{lesson:FA-C451-rahgozar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a bench, then the Persian for a resident.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رهگذر}}
\textbf{\fa{رهگذر}} (\emph{rahgozar}) — \textquotedblleft{}a passer-by\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{یک} \fa{رهگذر} \fa{راه} \fa{ایستگاه} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{ما} \fa{نشان} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Yek rahgozar râh-e istgâh râ be mâ neshân dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A passer-by showed us the way to the station.
\end{quote}

\emph{rah} (a short form of \emph{râh}) + \emph{gozar} 'passing'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rahgozar} is a native compound of \emph{rah}, a short form of \emph{râh} 'road' (Middle Persian \emph{rāh}, EtymDB), and \emph{gozar}, the present stem of \emph{gozashtan} 'to pass'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{همشهری} (hamshahri)}{همشهری (hamshahri)}]{\fa{همشهری} (hamshahri) — someone from the same town, a fellow townsman}

\label{lesson:FA-C451-hamshahri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a resident, then the Persian for a passer-by.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{همشهری}}
\textbf{\fa{همشهری}} (\emph{hamshahri}) — \textquotedblleft{}someone from the same town, a fellow townsman\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{فرودگاه} \fa{یک} \fa{همشهری} \fa{دیدم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar forudgâh yek hamshahri didam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At the airport I met someone from my home town.
\end{quote}

\emph{ham-} 'same' + \emph{shahr} 'town' + \emph{-i}. Also the name of a newspaper.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{hamshahri} is a native compound of \emph{ham-} 'same, together' and \emph{shahr} 'town', from Middle Persian \emph{šahr} (EtymDB), with the ending \emph{-i}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
